away.name: Semyon Varlamov
away.news: Varlamov made his season debut last week, returning to the crease for the first time in nearly two years, and will face the Ottawa Senators on Thursday. The veteran 38-year-old goalie shook off some rust, allowing three goals on 22 shots (.864 SV%) in a 5-2 loss to the New York Rangers, and hopes to return to form with one game under his belt. The Islanders enter action on Thursday as +144 road underdogs against a Senators team off to an impressive 5-2-0 start.

home.name: Daniil Tarasov
home.news: The struggling 1-3-2 Red Wings will turn to Tarasov to tend the twine for just the second time this season on Thursday against the Philadelphia Flyers. The 27-year-old Tarasov hasn't been called upon much this season, but he was excellent in his only outing, stopping all 30 shots he faced and recording a shutout in a 1-0 shootout loss to the Montreal Canadiens. Tarasov has a favourable matchup on Thursday against the Flyers, one of the few teams that have been more offensively challenged than the Red Wings, scoring just 10 goals in eight games (0-5-3).

home.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
home.news: Tampa Bay has scored fewer than two goals in three of six games this season (4-2-0), leaving little margin for error for the goaltending. That said, Vasilevskiy, the reigning 2025-26 Vezina Trophy winner, has performed below expectations so far, posting a 2.45 GAA and a lowly .886 SV% in five outings (3-2-0). Tampa Bay enters Thursday's contest as a significant -257 home favourite against the surprisingly potent early-season offence of the Seattle Kraken, who average 4.14 goals per game through seven games (5-2-0).

home.name: Akira Schmid
home.news: With Jacob Markstrom battling an undisclosed injury, Schmid will tend the twine Thursday against the Vancouver Canucks. Schmid is coming off his first win of the season, saving 24 of 27 shots (.889 SV%) in a 7-3 win over the Columbus Blue Jackets. The 26-year-old Swiss goalie has a 3.72 GAA and .875 SV% in three games this season (1-1-1). The Panthers enter Thursday's contest as significant -296 home favourites against a Vancouver Canucks team that has allowed a league-worst 38 goals through eight games (2-6-0).

away.name: Dylan Garand
away.news: The season-ending injury to Igor Shesterkin sparked panic among the Rangers faithful, but rookie Dylan Garand has been an impressive replacement so far. The 24-year-old Garand was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 25 of 26 shots (.962 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Tampa Bay Lightning. He has a stellar 1.15 GAA and .951 SV% in four games (3-1-0). The Rangers enter Thursday's contest as +117 road underdogs against a New Jersey Devils team that has scored fewer than two goals in three of their last five games (2-3-0).

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Wallstedt has been busy with Filip Gustavsson (hip) sidelined, and he got his first night off in Minnesota's previous game, but the team fared poorly without him, losing 5-2 to the Winnipeg Jets. Wallstedt emerged as Minnesota's starting goalie in the playoffs and has carried that momentum into the 2026-27 season. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie has an outstanding 1.82 GAA and .933 SV% in six games (4-1-1). Minnesota enters Thursday's contest as -140 home favourites against a St. Louis Blues team on a two-game winning streak.
